inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries: Information obtained during a DFPS investigation shows that the operation failed to notify parents of a less serious injury.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries (26 TAC §746.307(c))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: Information obtained during a DFPS investigation shows that the operation failed to assign a caregiver to an age group that matched their ability to safely and effectively meet the care of non-verbal children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments (26 TAC §746.1003(3))

occurrences.finding: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization: Information obtained throughout the investigation shows that the operation failed to report the incident to Child Care Regulation within 48 hours. The operation reported the incident via email, but did report by either speaking with someone or reporting on the abuse and neglect website within 48 hours.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.305(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Required Immunizations: 14 out of 17 children immunizations were not up to date.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Immunizations (26 TAC §746.613(a))

occurrences.finding: Nutrition and Food Service - Follow Meal Patterns: During snack time children were only served food from one food group which did not meet the USDA nutritional guidelines.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Nutrition and Food Service - Follow Meal Patterns (26 TAC §746.3301(b))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: Two caregivers did not know how many children they were responsible for.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact: Four out of ten children files were missing the address for the emergency contact.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact (26 TAC §746.605(6))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: A caregiver failed to wash an infant's hands after changing their diaper. This was corrected when the caregiver washed the infant's hands.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: Two classrooms had cleaning supplies that were accessible to children. This was corrected when the caregivers moved the cleaning supplies out of reach of children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: A caregiver without a background check eligibility letter had direct access to children in care. This was corrected when the caregiver did not return to the operation from their lunch break.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Information obtained throughout the investigation shows that the operation failed to demonstrate good judgement by continuously allowing children to enter a hallway closet that self locks and having to get a key to unlock the closet and let the children out.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two: Information obtained throughout the investigation shows that caregivers allowed children under the age of 2 years to participate in screen time activities.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two (26 TAC §746.2207(a))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: Operation did not have a current fire inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Annual Sanitation Inspection: Operation did not have a current sanitation report. This was corrected during my inspection when I received receipt of payment for the inspection to be completed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Sanitation Inspection (26 TAC §746.3401(a))

occurrences.finding: Medication Authorization Expires on First Anniversary: The medication authorization for a child requiring medication administration expired in April of 2024.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Medication Authorization Expires on First Anniversary (26 TAC §746.3803(b))

occurrences.finding: AP Must Place Infants in Face up Sleeping Position or Must Have Completed and Signed Sleep Exception Form for the Infant: A caregiver was observed placing a child in the crib on their stomach to nap. Caregiver was instructed to place the child in the crib on their back for nap.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Must Place Infants in Face up Sleeping Position or Must Have Completed and Signed Sleep Exception Form for the Infant (26 TAC §746.2427(a))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: Out of ten classrooms observed, three caregivers did not know the number children they were supervising.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: Two employees were present, going in the classroom hallway, and classrooms without completed background checks. One had an inactive status on their background check. One had a pending background check.    This was corrected when both employees left .
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Children from one class were observed running between rooms, standing on a table, and pulling each other by coats and blankets during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two: One classroom was using screen time with a child under the age of 2 years old.     This was corrected at inspection when the tablet was turned off.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two (26 TAC §746.2207(a))

occurrences.finding: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent: During an investigation it was found that the operation did not provide an incident report to the parent within the required 48 hours.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent (26 TAC §746.707)

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: During an investigation it was found that the operation waited multiple days to notify parents of children when they were made aware that a caregiver used prohibited punishment on their children while in care placing them at risk.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment: During an investigation it was found that a caregiver was leading a child to another table by pushing their head along the way, pushing children?s heads to a facedown position at tables, pushing a rolling bookshelf towards a child twice, and banging a tablet on a table by children.  There is evidence to suggest the caregiver restrains children by holding them tightly.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment (26 TAC §746.2805(1))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: During an investigation there is enough evidence to determine a caregiver was yelling at the children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: During an investigation a caregiver was observed moving two children by one of their arms, lifting them up off the floor to a new spot.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records- Training Hours: Six staff were lacking food allergy and hazardous material training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2912) (26 TAC §746.901(5))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: Three chidren were lacking the required immunizations.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages: Two caregivers were not aware of the children's ages in their care or where to obtain the information.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: A caregiver did not know how many children were in their care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times: Children were observed eating lunch and watching a movie.     Caregiver was informed why the television could not be on and the television was powered off.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times (26 TAC §746.2207(c)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: The caregiver did not show good judgment when she decided to carry a child in a football hold that led the child to sustaining a head injury.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Medical Authorization: One child did not have an emergency authorization on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Special Needs Statement (26 TAC §746.605(12))

occurrences.finding: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually: Four staff members who transport children are missing their transportation training certificate.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually (26 TAC §746.1316(a))

occurrences.finding: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep: Children were observed sleeping with their blankets over their heads in three separate classrooms.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep (26 TAC §746.2905(1))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training- Required Content: One caregiver did not have training in the following areas:  (1)Emergency preparedness ;  (2)Preventing and controlling the spread of communicable diseases, including   immunizations ;  (3)Administering medication, if applicable, including compliance with  ?746.3803 of this chapter (relating to What authorization must I obtain   before administering a medication to a child in my care?) ;  (4)Preventing and responding to emergencies due to food or an allergic   reaction ;  (5)Understanding building and physical premises safety, including   identification and protection from hazards that can cause bodily injury such   as electrical hazards, bodies of water, and vehicular traffic ; and  (6)Handling, storing, and disposing of hazardous materials including   compliance with ?746.3425 of this chapter (relating to Must caregivers   wear gloves when handling blood or bodily fluids containing blood?).
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))
